item.title: Design tokens
item.description:
All authored colour values in radiance live in assets/css/tokens.css. Every other stylesheet refers to the custom properties defined there, for example:

a {
  color: var(--radiance-accent);
}

Starting palette

The starting palette takes its cues from Ubuntu’s Radiance theme:

  • Pale panels with fine borders.
  • A deep aubergine desktop with purple and orange highlights.
  • An orange accent for links and selection.

These are starting values, not a guarantee of accessible contrast; adjust them when a combination needs improvement.

item.title: Getting started
item.description:
Prerequisites

radiance needs Hugo Extended 0.128.0 or newer. Check the installed version:

hugo version

Build the example site

The theme repository ships an example site:

hugo --source exampleSite --themesDir ../..

The command assumes the theme checkout directory is named radiance, so that ../.. resolves from exampleSite to the directory containing the theme.

Next steps

  • Read the other sample post listed under Posts.
  • Adjust the colours in assets/css/tokens.css.

item.title: About this site
item.description:
This example site demonstrates radiance, a Hugo theme that makes a content website feel like an Ubuntu desktop running GNOME 2.

The theme

  • The default light appearance is inspired by Ubuntu Radiance.
  • An Ambiance-inspired dark appearance is planned.
  • All authored colour values live in assets/css/tokens.css.

This site

The top panel provides Applications, Places and System menus; the applets on the right show the time, a link and a text meter. The sample posts cover getting started and the design tokens.
